sources.title: Decentralized route choice control of automated baggage handling systems
sources.authors: A. N. Tarau, B. De Schutter, J. Hellendoorn
sources.read_scope: Primary publisher abstract and author-PDF indexed abstract/introduction; direct PDF open returned Internal Error. No claim of full algorithm or experiment reproduction.
sources.finding: Local route control using decentralized MPC and heuristics trades computation against performance. The paper primarily studies loaded DCV routing, not a solved finite-tray reuse contract.
sources.mapping_inference: A local short-horizon forecast is a relevant baseline. Evaluate when coordination adds value over that baseline instead of calling decentralization itself a new contribution.

sources.title: Hierarchical route control in DCV-based baggage handling systems
sources.read_scope: Author-PDF indexed introduction and modeling scope only.
sources.finding: The authors distinguish no-communication decentralized control from communicating distributed control; their loaded-routing study assumes sufficient DCVs at loading stations.
sources.mapping_inference: Do not adopt the sufficient-cart assumption. For G31, preserve finite physical tray availability and use the broader user meaning of decentralized operation, explicitly reporting which messages are exchanged.

sources.title: An Integrated Model Predictive Scheme for Baggage-Handling Systems: Routing, Line Balancing, and Empty-Cart Management
sources.authors: Y. Zeinaly, B. De Schutter, H. Hellendoorn
sources.read_scope: Author 17-page PDF text: abstract, introductory loaded/empty distinction, assumptions on page4, loading/unloading conservation, state description, empty-flow cost and A-LP. No full derivation verification, optimizer reproduction or new novelty discovery; already present in repository prior-art ledger.
sources.finding: Joint loaded routing, empty management and line balancing already exist. Continuous flows, sampled link times and LP horizon assumptions differ from G31's discrete trays and events.
sources.mapping_inference: Use supply conservation and shared capacity in a fair joint MPC baseline. Any aggregate relaxation is a proposal or bound until decoded into legal discrete native requests; never a replacement for the physical verifier.

sources.title: Lifelong Multi-Agent Path Finding for Online Pickup and Delivery Tasks
sources.authors: H. Ma, J. Li, T. K. Satish Kumar, S. Koenig
sources.finding: Token Passing and task swaps address online pickup/delivery and have well-formed-instance conditions.
sources.mapping_inference: Useful task/route coordination reference. A token or task swap is not automatically legal under fixed G31 FIFO, source ownership and immutable issued actions.

sources.title: Priority Inheritance with Backtracking for Iterative Multi-agent Path Finding
sources.authors: K. Okumura, M. Machida, X. Defago, Y. Tamura
sources.read_scope: Primary paper indexed abstract/introduction and author abstract; no new algorithm reproduction.
sources.finding: Local communication supports fast iterative movement coordination. Finite-time guarantees require graph conditions.
sources.mapping_inference: Existing G31 movement coordination remains the executor; do not modify the user's parent bounded_local_pibt.hpp. Empty supply selection is an additional planning problem. Directed closed edges and Storage/FIFO do not inherit PIBT guarantees.
